newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - drifts 1/4 to 3/8 lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - drifts 1/4 to 3/8 lower.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices drifted lower throughout the day Monday, losing about 1/4 to 3/8 point in quiet action, traders said.

With no real action in the primary or secondary markets and no key data releases Monday, the tone was "cautious," one trader said, adding that the lack of follow-through from last week's gains prompted some profit taking.
"We've got nothing going on here 'til Friday," the trader said, referring to the September Producer Price Index and retail sales figures set for release at the end of the week.
The Treasury long bond was also suffering profit taking, off 14/32 heading into the New York close. The yield moved to 6.79 percent.

In the muni secondary, Denver Airport MBIA 5-1/2s of 2025 were bid at a 5.78 percent yield, up five basis points from Friday. Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority 5-5/8s of 2026 were up one basis point to 5.78 percent net.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract closed down 26/32 to 115-15/32 and the December T-bond fell 17/32 to 111-5/32. The MOB spread narrowed nine ticks from Friday to 138 ticks.
In the new issue market, Goldman Sachs & Co said it repriced and restructured $116.6 million Washington Public Power Supply System refunding revenue bonds, for Nuclear Project No 1.
At the repricing, Goldman adjusted yields in several maturities but left the top yield in 2017 unchanged at 5.82 percent.

Merrill Lynch & Co said it had a $20.2 million balance on Oak Ridge, Tenn.'s $16 million general obligation and $7 million electric system revenue bond issues. Merrill won the deals in competitive bidding Monday.

Tuesday primary market deals include Wisconsin's $100 million health bond issue through senior manager Merrill Lynch & Co. That deal tops a list totaling about $422 million of negotiated offerings expected Tuesday.
On the competitive list are 18 sales totaling $195 million, including a $58.6 million Virginia Housing Development Authority deal set for 1100 EDT.
Tuesday data releases are sparse, but the Treasury plans to auction $10 billion of 10-year notes.
